questions.q: What does Power Automate let an organisation do?
options: Optimise business processes and automate repetitive tasks
questions.explain: Flows connect apps and services to sync files, send notifications, collect data and more.
questions.evidence: Power Automate allows you to optimize your business processes across your organization and automate repetitive tasks.

questions.q: Why can people build automated workflows with little or no coding knowledge?
options: Its intuitive interface and many connectors
It only works with Microsoft Excel
Workflows are written by an AI for you
It requires a certified developer licence
questions.explain: Drag-and-drop components and prebuilt connectors do most of the work.
questions.evidence: Its intuitive interface and many connectors allow you to create workflows with little to no knowledge of coding.

questions.q: What do desktop flows add to Power Automate?
options: Robotic process automation (RPA) to automate repetitive desktop processes
questions.explain: Desktop flows can be recorded or built with drag-and-drop actions.
questions.evidence: Desktop flows broaden the existing robotic process automation (RPA) capabilities in Power Automate and enable you to automate all repetitive desktop processes.

questions.q: What is process mining?
options: Technology that helps businesses understand their real processes and find opportunities for improvement and automation
questions.explain: It analyses event data to show how processes are actually executed.
questions.evidence: Process mining is a research area and technology that helps businesses understand their real processes, how they're operated, and identify opportunities for improvement, automation, and digitalization.

questions.q: What is a weakness of desktop-based RPA compared with API-based connectors?
options: It is susceptible to breaking when things change, such as updates or new screen layouts
questions.explain: APIs are kept stable by vendors; screen layouts are not.
questions.evidence: RPA is susceptible to breaking when things change, such as when updates are applied to a local computer's environment or the layout of an application's screens.

questions.q: When should you choose a desktop application automation?
options: When no connector exists and the system is a desktop application on a PC
When the process runs once a year
questions.explain: Check the list of connectors first; fall back to desktop automation only when needed.
questions.evidence: If you can't find a connector, and if the system is a desktop application on a PC, this is the automation method to use.

questions.q: What is an unattended automation scenario?
options: A user watches the automation run on their own screen
Nobody is allowed to see the results
The automation runs only when an error occurs
A designated computer or server runs the automation on behalf of a user
questions.explain: Attended automations run while the user is at the computer; unattended ones run without them.
questions.evidence: a designated computer or a server is set up to run the automation on behalf of a user.

questions.q: According to the guidance, what is one benefit of automating repetitive processes?
options: It removes the need for managers
It helps employees avoid mental and physical burnout
It eliminates the need for testing
questions.explain: Automation frees people for higher-value work.
questions.evidence: Automating repetitive processes can help your employees avoid mental and physical burnout.

questions.q: What should you always design into an automation?
options: As many steps as possible in one flow
A plan B so the business process can continue even if the automation doesn't work
A dependency on one person's account
questions.explain: Smaller flows and fallbacks make automations easier to maintain and safer to run.
questions.evidence: You should always design your automation so that there's a plan B—to make sure your business process can continue even if the automation doesn't work.

questions.q: Why should you test all possible patterns and outcomes of a flow?
options: A flow might not simply fail — it might run but produce unexpected results
Testing is required to publish any flow
questions.explain: Silent wrong results can be worse than visible failures.
questions.evidence: your flow might not simply fail, it might run but produce unexpected results.

questions.q: What can Power Automate workflows between apps and services do?
options: Synchronise files, get notifications, collect data and more
questions.explain: Flows connect your apps so repetitive work happens automatically.
questions.evidence: This service helps you create automated workflows between your favorite apps and services to synchronize files, get notifications, collect data, and more.

questions.q: Why do many organisations use separate environments in Power Automate?
options: To keep flows in development apart from those ready for wide use
questions.explain: Some organisations also separate environments by department.
questions.evidence: Many organizations use environments to separate flows that are still being developed from those that are ready for widespread use.

questions.q: In which ways can you create a flow in Power Automate?
options: With Copilot, from a template, or by building your own
questions.explain: Templates give a quick start for common scenarios.
questions.evidence: Create flows by using Copilot, templates or build your own

questions.q: You create a flow in one environment. Can you see it from another environment?
questions.explain: Environments keep their flows, apps and data separate.
questions.evidence: When you create a flow in one environment, you aren't able to see it from another environment.

questions.q: Who can access the default environment?
questions.explain: Other environments can be restricted to certain people.
questions.evidence: Every member in an organization can access the default environment

questions.q: What should you check before creating a flow or an app?
options: That the flow has a logo
That you have printed the template
That you are in the correct environment
questions.explain: Use the environment switcher in the header to check.
questions.evidence: Make sure that you're in the correct environment before you create a flow, an app, or a similar component.

questions.q: How does process mining show how processes are really carried out?
options: By analysing event data from various sources
By guessing from the org chart
questions.explain: Real execution data often differs from the documented process.
questions.evidence: By analyzing event data from various sources, the process mining capability provides a clear view of how processes are actually being executed in practice.

questions.q: How can process mining improve operational efficiency?
questions.explain: Organisations can then streamline operations and improve productivity.
questions.evidence: Process mining can help identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies in processes

questions.q: What is the first step when planning an automation project?
options: Plan: identify the who, what, when and why
questions.explain: Design, build, test and deploy follow.
questions.evidence: Identify the who, what, when, and why

questions.q: What can Power Automate unify?
options: Cloud services, desktop applications and legacy systems
questions.explain: That breadth lets one flow span old and new systems.
questions.evidence: you can use to unify cloud services, desktop applications, and legacy systems

questions.q: How do modern applications give programmatic access to their data and functions?
questions.explain: Connectors are built on these APIs.
questions.evidence: Modern applications (including cloud-based services) use APIs to provide programmatic access to data and functionality.

questions.q: What can software engineers create for any application with an API?
questions.explain: Custom connectors extend automation to systems without a ready-made connector.
questions.evidence: software engineers can create new, custom connectors to any application that has an API available

questions.q: What do connectors let you do in an automation?
options: Access data and use application functionality without writing code
questions.explain: Desktop-based RPA is the fallback when no connector or API exists.
questions.evidence: Without writing any code yourself, you can use connectors to access data and use a wide variety of application functionality in your automation.

questions.q: After finding a connector for your system, what should you check?
options: That it has a nice icon
That it was released this year
That the actions you need are available for it
questions.explain: A connector may exist but lack the specific action you need.
questions.evidence: After you find the connector, make sure that the actions you need are available for that connector.

questions.q: What comes after process design in an automation project?
options: Architectural design — deciding how to automate the process
questions.explain: This is where you choose connectors, custom connectors or desktop automation.
questions.evidence: After the process design is complete, the next step is architectural design, where you focus on how you'll automate that process.

questions.q: How does a custom connector interact with a target system?
options: By clicking on the screen like a user
questions.explain: UI-based desktop automation is used when there is no API.
questions.evidence: A custom connector allows the automation to interact with the target system via a published API.

questions.q: What is the first step in designing a process automation?
options: Deciding when and what to automate
questions.explain: Then identify which part of the current process to automate.
questions.evidence: When you design a process automation, the first step is to decide when and what to automate.

questions.q: Which processes should be high on your list for automation?
options: Processes done the same way every time
questions.explain: Repetitive processes are predictable and tiring for people.
questions.evidence: Processes that are done the same way every time should be high on your list to consider for automation.

questions.q: Which tasks are prone to human error and good candidates for automation?
options: Copying values between systems or keying in data from paper forms
questions.explain: Automation removes the risk of typos and missed fields.
questions.evidence: Tasks like copying and pasting values from one system to another, or keying in data from paper forms, are processes where human errors can occur.

questions.q: Why build several smaller flows instead of one large flow?
questions.explain: A change to one step need not suspend the whole process.
questions.evidence: There are several reasons why you should make multiple, smaller flows: Maintenance is easier.

questions.q: When an automation fails, who receives repair tips?
options: Whoever created or owns the automation
questions.explain: Flow Checker also helps find and fix errors.
questions.evidence: If your automation fails, repair tips are automatically sent to whoever created or owns the automation.

questions.q: When deploying an automation, what should you plan in order to avoid disruption?
options: How to delete the old data
How to stop all work for a week
How to keep the change secret
How the new automation will replace the current business process
questions.explain: A planned switch-over keeps the business running.
questions.evidence: it's important to consider how you'll replace the current business process with the new automation, to avoid disrupting the business

questions.q: Why add co-owners to a flow?
options: So they can update it in your absence
questions.explain: Your manager is a sensible co-owner.
questions.evidence: Make sure you add a couple of co-owners so that they can update the flow in your absence.

questions.q: Who might have guidelines for flow ownership in your company?
options: The Power Platform Center of Excellence
questions.explain: A CoE sets standards for using the platform across the organisation.
questions.evidence: If your company has a Center of Excellence for Microsoft Power Platform, they might have guidelines for flow ownership.

questions.q: What does safety mean for an AI agent, according to the lesson?
options: That the agent performs as designed
That it never uses the internet
That it runs without any prompts
That it is always the fastest option
questions.explain: Builders have methods and tools to maximise safety.
questions.evidence: Safety means that the AI agent performs as designed.

questions.q: What is a meta system message used for?
options: An LLM uses it to generate the system prompts for the agents you create
questions.explain: A system message framework makes prompts scalable.
questions.evidence: Step 1: Create a Meta System Message The meta prompt will be used by an LLM to generate the system prompts for the agents we create.

questions.q: Which kind of measures help ensure data and access are properly managed when building agents?
questions.explain: Security is a key consideration for agents.
questions.evidence: Implement security measures to ensure that data and access are properly managed.

questions.q: What is the first step in planning for an AI agent?
options: Choosing the colour of the interface
Defining a clear overall goal and breaking the task into manageable tasks
questions.explain: Clear goals and decomposition make agents reliable.
questions.evidence: Introduction This lesson will cover Defining a clear overall goal and breaking a complex task into manageable tasks.

questions.q: Why use structured output in agent planning?
options: For more reliable and machine-readable responses
To avoid using a language model
questions.explain: Structured output can be checked and passed between steps.
questions.evidence: Leveraging structured output for more reliable and machine-readable responses.

questions.q: What should you do with a complex task when planning an agent?
options: Give it all to the agent at once
Ask the user to do it
Decompose it into manageable subtasks in a logical sequence
questions.explain: Then evaluate outcomes and iterate.
questions.evidence: Decompose a complex task into manageable subtasks and organize them into a logical sequence.

questions.q: When do you need to consider the multi-agent design pattern?
options: As soon as a project involves multiple agents
questions.explain: It is not always clear when to switch to multiple agents.
questions.evidence: As soon as you start working on a project that involves multiple agents, you will need to consider the multi-agent design pattern.

questions.q: Which question does the multi-agent lesson ask about visibility?
options: How many colours should the dashboard use?
How do we have visibility to how the multiple agents are interacting with each other?
Which agent has the best name?
How long should each prompt be?
questions.explain: Observing interactions is a building block of multi-agent systems.
questions.evidence: How do we have visibility to how the multiple agents are interacting with each other?
